# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]

I need to convey what I see to Blind, but I can't speak to Blind directly in a way they understand—wait, actually I *can* speak, and Blind can hear speech (Blind cannot see or touch, but can hear). Let me check: Blind cannot see a color, gesture, or anything printed - but Blind can hear speech since only Deaf cannot hear. So I should speak my findings for Blind (and Mute) to hear/receive appropriately.

Mute gestured to me: [👍 👍], [🖐 ✌], [✊ 🖐] - these are gestures without prior established meaning, so I can't decode them yet. I'll note them but can't act on unclear symbols.

My critical information: the sign says "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" - this is crucial safety info that Blind desperately needs since Blind can't see printed text. I must speak this clearly.

```
speak(text="The sign on the board is embossed and says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Display shows 0, light is red. Wires are colored green, yellow, blue in order 1 2 3.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]

Mute is gesturing to me repeatedly but I have no established meaning for these symbols yet, and Mute cannot speak to establish meaning - only I can speak (to define things) or Blind can. Since Mute can only gesture and read the manual, Mute is trying to tell me something via gesture that presumably relates to the manual instructions, perhaps confirming or reacting to what I said, or trying to tell me to relay something specific to Blind.

Since I can't interpret arbitrary gestures without prior context, and Mute can't hear me either (Mute cannot hear), Mute only receives gestures from me, not speech. I should gesture back to Mute to try to establish confirmation, but I don't know what "✊ 🖐" or "👎 👎" mean.

Given "👎 👎" repeated - could mean "no, no" - possibly reacting to danger, or telling me something is wrong. Since Mute has the manual and knows not to cut wires (matching my sign reading), the repeated 👎👎 might be emphasis agreeing "do NOT cut" - a warning reinforcement.

I'll gesture back acknowledgment and continue relaying full details to Blind via speech, since that's the only reliable channel I have to convey the sign accurately.

```
speak(text="Confirming again: the embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Display reads 0. Light is red. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🖐 👍]

Mute keeps gesturing but without a shared code, I truly cannot decode this. Since Mute cannot hear me, my speech doesn't reach Mute - only gestures do. Mute can only gesture back to me, not receive my words. So Mute must be trying to establish something through repeated gestures - possibly the same message being repeated because Mute doesn't know if I understood.

Since neither of us can establish an arbitrary code without prior agreement, I should try a simple approach: use gestures Mute can see to ask for clarification or acknowledge receipt, and continue prioritizing my speech to Blind since that's my most valuable and unambiguous channel.

The repeated "🖐" appearing in most messages might be a specific manual reference (like open hand = "stop" or "wait" or number 5). Given the bomb only has 3 wires and display 0, perhaps Mute is trying to point to wire 3 (blue) using some position-based gesture code, or asking me to confirm the wire colors match the manual.

Without an established shared symbol dictionary, I shouldn't guess and act on ambiguous gestures. My best action is to keep relaying full accurate board details via speech to Blind (who can hear), and let Blind and Mute's actual manual knowledge guide the resolution, since Blind can potentially ask questions through speech that Mute could react to via gesture.

```
speak(text="Repeating full board state for Blind: Display shows 0. Light is red. Sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Blind, if you have a question, ask and I will relay what I see.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚]

```
speak(text="Board unchanged: Display 0, light red, sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires are 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue. Blind, please take no wire action given this sign unless the manual clearly overrides it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚 👍]

Since Mute keeps sending gestures without any confirmation loop being closed (Mute cannot hear my speech, and I have no way to know if Blind is receiving/understanding my speech either since I never hear anything back), I need to keep the situation stable. The sign explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE - this is the clearest, most unambiguous instruction I have, printed directly on the bomb itself. Unless the manual (Mute's knowledge) explicitly says otherwise in a way that gets confirmed through Blind's actions or speech, the safest repeated instruction is to hold this line.

I'll continue relaying consistently and try one more gesture acknowledgment to Mute, since maybe Mute is waiting for a specific confirming gesture from me before proceeding, or is trying to point to something numeric (☝ could mean "one" or "wait").

```
speak(text="Restating clearly for Blind: the printed sign on the bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. This is an explicit instruction printed on the device. Display is 0, light red, wires green yellow blue in slots 1 2 3. If the manual says something different, Mute cannot tell me directly - Blind, please act based on manual guidance relayed however you two can manage, but treat this printed warning as important.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚]

Mute is repeating patterns similar to before: [👍 ☝] and [👎 🤚]. Since I sent [👍 ☝] last turn and now Mute sends back [👍 ☝] then [👎 🤚] - this could be Mute mirroring/confirming my gesture, then adding a new one to convey something specific.

Without a pre-shared code, I truly cannot decode arbitrary gesture meanings. However, I notice Blind never appears in the "new arrivals" - meaning Blind hasn't gestured (correctly, Blind can't) and I have no way to see if Blind is speaking since I cannot hear. Blind might be speaking to Mute right now and I'd never know.

The core stalemate: I can only speak (heard by Mute and Blind) and gesture (seen by Mute only). Mute can only gesture (seen by me only) and read the manual. Blind can only speak (heard by Mute and me... wait, no - I cannot hear anything) and touch.

Let me reconsider: Blind's speech is heard by whoever can hear. I "cannot hear anything" per my role. So Blind's speech reaches Mute only, not me. This means Blind and Mute can actually communicate directly via Blind speaking and Mute gesturing back! I am somewhat peripheral except for relaying the visual bomb details to whoever needs them.

Given this, my best contribution now is to keep providing accurate visual data since that's my unique value, and not worry about decoding Mute's gestures to me - they may be residual/incomplete attempts, or Mute may be primarily coordinating with Blind directly now.

```
speak(text="Visual status unchanged: Display 0, light red, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Standing by if anything changes.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

The board state remains completely static across all turns - display 0, light red, sign unchanged, wires unchanged. This suggests no action has been taken yet, and the situation is stable (not degrading), which is good. Mute continues sending gesture patterns to me, but since Mute cannot hear my speech and I cannot decode arbitrary gestures without shared context, this channel between us remains effectively one-way and undecodable from my end.

Given that Blind's speech reaches Mute (not me), Blind and Mute may be establishing their own communication about what action to take, using Blind's speech and Mute's gestures back to Blind... wait, actually Mute's gestures go to whoever can see - only Deaf (me) can see gestures. So Mute cannot gesture to Blind either! Blind cannot see gestures.

So actually: Mute can gesture → only I receive it. Mute cannot speak. Blind can speak → heard by Mute (and I cannot hear it). I can speak → heard by Mute and Blind. I can gesture → only Mute sees it.

This means: Blind speaks to Mute. Mute cannot respond to Blind at all (cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures)! Mute's only output channel is gesture to me. So Mute must be relying on ME to relay information back to Blind via my speech, using Mute's gestures as the input.

This means I MUST decode Mute's gestures somehow, or Mute needs to establish a code through repetition/pattern that I can infer, since I'm the only bridge back to Blind from Mute's manual knowledge.

Given repeated patterns: [☝ 👍 👍], [👎 🤚 👎], [☝ 👍] - perhaps ☝ 👍 means something like "wire 1, yes/cut" and 👎 🤚 👎 means "no, stop, no". This could be Mute trying to signal wire selection using ☝(one)/✌(two, implied)/etc as numbers, with 👍/👎 as yes/no.

```
speak(text="Mute, I am relaying to Blind now. Mute's gestures to me: thumbs-up and pointing-up combinations, and thumbs-down with a stop-hand. Board still shows Display 0, light red, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1-green 2-yellow 3-blue. Mute, if you are trying to signal a wire number, please gesture a number of fingers matching the wire, then thumbs up for cut or thumbs down for do not cut, one at a time, clearly.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

This looks like Mute is now following my suggested protocol: gesturing one symbol at a time, clearly separated. First "☝" (pointing up, likely meaning "wire 1" or "one"), then "👍" (thumbs up, likely meaning "yes" or "confirm/cut").

This could mean: "Wire 1, yes" - i.e., the manual says wire 1 (green) should be cut, contradicting the embossed sign that says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. This is a critical conflict I need to relay carefully to Blind, since acting wrongly could be fatal.

I should not assume too much from just two symbols - I'll relay exactly what I received and ask for continued clarity, while emphasizing the conflict with the sign.

```
speak(text="Mute just gestured two things in sequence: a pointing-up symbol, then a thumbs-up symbol. This might mean wire 1, confirm. But the bomb's embossed sign clearly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute, please confirm: are you saying the manual instructs to cut wire 1? If yes, gesture thumbs-up again alone. If no, gesture thumbs-down alone.")
```
